cohort.governedBy: former CPL § 160.55, through a motion to enter or enforce the omitted legacy sealing order
cohort.basis: This cohort is not literally within the 'prior to the effective date' language of current § 160.55(3). Before November 1, 1991 sealing depended on the court-generated sealing process then required by § 160.55. The 1991 amendment added the modern rule under which the disposition report itself supplies the sealing notice, and renumbered the prior provisions. New York Courts nevertheless instructs people with pre-November 1, 1991 convictions to ask the terminating court to seal the records.
cohort.instrument: Motion to Enter and Enforce a Legacy Sealing Order Under Former CPL § 160.55
cohort.instrumentTitleIsDescriptive: This is a legally descriptive motion title, not the name of an approved statewide form. No current statute supplies a specially named clerk application for this cohort. Request entry of the sealing order that should have accompanied the disposition under the law then in effect, and the relief described in current § 160.55(1).
cohort.doNotInvokeModernProcess: Do not attempt to invoke the modern automatic-reporting process as though it applied at the original disposition, and do not apply the current automatic clerk-report mechanism as the initiating procedure.
cohort.noticeRule: No current statewide statute supplies a separate legacy notice period. Serve the district attorney and comply with the terminating court's local criminal-motion return-date and service rules. 20 days may be used as a conservative operational minimum only where consistent with local practice, and must not be stated as an express statutory requirement for this cohort.
cohort.additionalAllegation: The motion must state the historical failure to enter or transmit the sealing order required by the law governing the disposition.

actor: The person who was convicted of the qualifying violation or traffic infraction, acting personally or through counsel. For the pre-September 1980 cohort, § 160.55(3) expressly gives the person the right to move; official court guidance likewise directs people with pre-November 1991 convictions to ask the court.
destination: The court in which the criminal action or proceeding terminated, using the original docket or case number where available. If the original court no longer exists or its records have been transferred, court administration must identify the successor court or record custodian before the motion is generated.
